text_blocks.snippet: Early signs of type 2 diabetes develop gradually and include increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue.
snippet_highlighted_words: increased thirst, frequent urination, and constant fatigue

list.snippet: Increased thirst and frequent urination: High blood sugar forces your kidneys to work harder to filter and absorb excess glucose, pulling water from your tissues and making you go to the bathroom more often—especially at night.
Persistent fatigue: Because your cells cannot properly absorb glucose from your bloodstream for energy, you may feel deeply exhausted even after sleeping.
Increased hunger: Your body misses out on cellular energy, triggering constant hunger even right after finishing a meal.
Blurred vision: Fluctuating fluid levels can cause the lenses in your eyes to swell, changing their shape and making it hard to focus.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: High blood sugar impairs blood circulation and weakens your immune system, causing minor injuries to take weeks or months to heal.
Tingling or numbness: Peripheral nerve damage can start as a mild prickly or numb sensation in your hands and feet.
Darkened skin patches: Velvety, dark patches of skin in body folds like the neck, armpits, or groin—known as acanthosis nigricans—frequently signal underlying insulin resistance.
